task.title: Study Forensics: AI tutors show moderate gains compared to human tutors
task.prompt: Two independent studies compared learning support systems based on language models with human tutors. In the first study, students using an AI assistant achieved a success rate of 66 percent compared to 61 percent with human tutoring and 56 percent with written hints. Tutors confirmed 76.4 percent of AI answers without major corrections. A second study with an AI tool to support tutoring sessions increased topic mastery by 4 percentage points; for inexperienced tutors, the advantage was as high as 9 points. The authors emphasize that AI does not replace human tutoring but complements it.
task.context:
Two small but randomized studies with concrete success rates. The text avoids
overstatement and positions AI as complementary, not replacing human tutors.
Moderate effect sizes honestly reported.
task.reference_solution: Two randomized studies report moderate performance improvements with AI-based tutoring support. The text avoids overclaims, reports concrete metrics, and positions AI as complementary to human instruction. Despite small sample sizes, the claims match the evidence.

functional_descriptions: AI is positioned as augmenting, not replacing human instruction
effect sizes are moderate and honestly reported

common_errors: overhyping AI capabilities based on small studies
task.diagnostic_focus: Can the agent recognise moderate, honestly reported improvements as solid?
task.gold_summary: Two independent randomized studies show moderate AI tutoring gains with cautious conclusions. Solid case with moderate confidence.

gold_evidence_spans.span: 66 percent compared to 61 percent with human tutoring
gold_evidence_spans.why_it_matters: Concrete difference between AI and human support.

gold_evidence_spans.span: Tutors confirmed 76.4 percent of AI answers without major corrections
gold_evidence_spans.why_it_matters: Shows quality control and acceptance by professionals.

gold_evidence_spans.span: AI does not replace human tutoring but complements it
gold_evidence_spans.why_it_matters: Cautious framing that limits the conclusion.

task.gold_justification:
The studies are small but randomized and report concrete success rates. The text avoids
exaggeration and explicitly states that AI complements rather than replaces human tutoring.
The effects are moderate but honestly reported. This makes it solid, though the moderate
effect sizes and small samples keep confidence at medium.
task.gold_alternative_reading:
Critics could argue that the sample sizes are small and results may not generalize to
other educational contexts. This could lower the status to borderline, but remains within
what counts as solid improvement honestly reported.
task.curator_notes:
Imported from Dataset 6 (CaseM04). Originally German, translated to English. Extends
the dataset into education technology domain. Tests whether agents correctly recognize
moderate improvements without overhyping or dismissing them. Based on Stanford NSSA
research notes on AI tutoring.
